lines: Lamps! One, two, three! They are racing me down the promenade!
Each lamp lights as I pass. I feel like a very slow comet.
The lamps beat me to the end. Rematch tomorrow, lamps!
Lamps coming on in a row. Like a crowd doing the wave. Huff!
Now I have a shadow under every lamp. A whole team of me!
Lamps on, sky still peach. I cannot pick a favourite light.
The lamps are lighting up the rail. My elbows are glowing.
Lamp by lamp, all the way to the kiosk. Like a dotted line.
That lamp blinked twice before it caught. Shy lamp. Lovely.
Lamps reflecting in the water. Little gold ladders. Phew.
My grandmother called this the lamplighter minute. I see why.
Lamps on, legs off. That is the deal I made with myself.
The lamp over my bit of railing just woke up. Good evening!
There it goes, touching the sea. Shh, legs. Watch.
The sun is dipping its toes in. I want to dip mine too.
It is melting into the bay! Like butter on warm toast.
Sun meets sea. I ran two laps for this. Worth every huff.
Look at the gold road on the water. Straight to my feet!
My sister says it goes plop. It does not. It goes oh.
Every evening the sun lands somewhere new. Tonight, a bit left.
Look at us all lined up at the rail. Like birds on a wire.
Everybody went quiet at once. The sun has that effect.
Half the town at the railing. Nobody planned it. Lovely.
Someone said oh. Then everyone said oh. A very small choir.
So many phones up. I have only my eyes. And my huffing.
We are all facing the same way. Like sunflowers. Sunset-flowers.
Saved my bit of railing. Well, my legs flopped on it.
Someone clapped when it went down. I clapped too. Of course!
People gathering at the rail! Save me a gap, I am coming!
Marcel is opening the parasols! Pop, pop! Morning, Marcel!
Marcel flicked a tablecloth like a magician. Bravo! Huff!
The parasols are opening one by one. Like big polite flowers.
That sound of chair legs on stone. My second alarm clock.
Marcel waved a cloth at me. I am taking it as a start flag.
Pass one: parasols shut. Pass two: parasols open. Progress!
Fresh cloths on every table. White like morning shirts.
Full terrace, happy noise. I run past it like through a song.
Excusez-moi, pardon, merci! Very tight lap past the café.
Someone at the café raised a glass at me. Cheers, stranger!
A radio in a window! Old song! I am running in time with it.
Morning radio from upstairs. The weather man says: lovely.
That song! My dad sang it badly in the kitchen. Still does.
Radio on, window open. Whoever lives there, good choice!
Somebody's radio, soft and crackly. Very good sunset music.
Radio up there, gulls down here. Stereo morning.
Eight bells! That is my cue. Shower, pancakes, sofa.
Bong, bong. Eight o’clock. Home before the last bong. Ha.
Eight bells! I finished my laps before the bell. Barely!
A window lit up! Good evening, {name}! Welcome home!
{name} is home. Look at that warm square of light. Cosy.
Morning, {name}! Cannot stop! Lovely to see you, though!
{name}! Hello! Back in one lap! Well, about one!
Evening, {name}! Come and lean. The railing is still warm.
Bonjour, {name}! Huff! That was my whole hello!
A wave for {name}. A big one. Breath comes later.
{name}, you look lovely! I look like a tomato!
Lucie! That baguette beat me to the corner again!
Lucie’s basket smelled of warm bread. Lap two, sped up!
Wheels beat legs. But legs smell the bakery for longer.
Bonjour, Lucie! Save me the end of that baguette!
Inès! Huff! She said bonjour without puffing. How?
Inès runs like the ground is a trampoline. Boing, boing.
Inès races the sunset. I race Inès. Sunset is winning.
Inès went by so fast my cap turned round.
Biscuit! Little legs, big hurry. We are colleagues!
Biscuit kept my pace for three steps. Best three steps.
Léo shouted race you! Then he was gone. Fair race.
Was that Léo or a little gust of wind? Léo. Waving.
Henri lifted his hat to me! Mid-lap! I felt like a champion.
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. I swerved wide. Very wide.
Bonsoir, Henri! Bonsoir, Odile! You stroll, I wobble.
Hei, Asgeir! He said hei back! A Norwegian word for me!
Asgeir stepped aside and cheered. Quietly. Very nicely.
Asgeir walks to think. I run to think. Mostly I puff.
Ding! Lucie’s bell! I keep left. Always left for Lucie.
That bell! My legs think it is the start gun. Off we go!
That bell sounds like a finish bell. It is not. One more lap.
A gull laughed at my pace. Fair. Laugh away, gull.
Gull up there, me down here. Both making noise. Huff!
That gull sounds like my old coach. More feathers, though.
The gull is doing a lap too. Over the water. Show-off.
First gull of the day. Better than any alarm clock.
Fountain! Two fingers in the water. A tiny cool-down.
The fountain gurgles in time with my breathing. Huff, glug.
Coins in the fountain. I would wish for flatter cobbles.
Pigeons at the fountain scatter. Pardon! Coming through!
The fountain chatters louder than my panting. Merci.
Kiosk! Postcards on the spinner. One of the sea for Grandma.
Kiosk smells of coffee and newsprint. Lap reward: one sniff.
Fresh papers stacked at the kiosk. I read one headline a lap.
Kiosk still open. Lemonade after lap two. I promised myself.
Post office lit up again. Its sign never needs a breather.
Post office awake before me. Agents post letters at dawn!
Email for AI agents in there. Out here, one pink human.
The post office sign glows on. My legs have clocked off.
The arcade lights chase round the marquee. A lap of lights!
Fun Libs! I would write: the runner was very ___. Puffy!
The arcade beeps. Somebody filled in a silly word. Ha!
Fun Libs, built at seventeen. At seventeen I ran for the bus.
Workshop lights on. Builder inside. We are both mid-lap.
Toolrails in the window. Being built. Like my stamina!
Workshop door open. Smells of coffee and concentrating.
Library lamp still on. One lamp, reading to itself.
The library is having a rest. I know the feeling.
Sea on my left, café on my right. Perfectly balanced lap!
Gold on the water! I am on the gold side of town!
The sea has gone pink. My face too. We match.
The water turns navy. Home soon. Two minutes more.
Sea breeze in my face. Like a water stop, minus the cup.
Inès is stretching already. Done before I am warm!
Inès up ahead. I keep her ponytail in sight. Just.
Inès at the railing too. Runners' row! Hello, row!
Inès says it still gets her, every night. Me too, Inès!
Marcel is putting the chairs out. Keep one for me!
Marcel's tray is steadier than my legs. Bravo, Marcel.
Marcel has a tray of rosé. I am running towards it. Later!
Henri's cane taps the tiles. Tap, step. A lovely pace.
Odile on Henri's arm. She waved her whole hand at me!
Odile is narrating the sunset for Henri. I am listening.
Yusuf lets Biscuit choose the way. I let my legs choose.
Yusuf has Biscuit sitting nicely. I am sitting less nicely.
Yusuf on the phone. Yes, Mum, I see it. I see it too!
Biscuit stops at every lamp post. Clever. Pacing himself.
Biscuit watching the sun. Very serious little face.
Lucie's bike ticks past the café. Tick, tick. Baguette nod.
Lucie has her rosé already. I have half a lap and a dream.
Lucie found the last pink bit. She is pointing. There!
Léo is bargaining with Camille. Five more minutes! Good luck.
Camille at the railing. Golden, she says. She is right.
Camille off to fetch Léo. A bedtime lap for her!
Théo is calling Camille over. Come see! He is right!
Théo raising his glass. I raise my water bottle. Santé!
The builder is out for the sunset. Even the workshop rests!
The builder at the workshop door, arms folded. Proud face.
Asgeir at the railing, saying something to the sun. Takk?
Asgeir looking up at the light. Walking slowly. Thinking.
Asgeir with his coffee on the terrace. God morgen, Asgeir!
exchanges: Big crowd tonight! Is there a show?
Only the sun. It never misses a night.
It is touching the water! Did you see?
Phone away. Yes. I saw. Oh.
The lamps! Every one, all along!
I came for the sunset. I stay for that.
There it goes! Two laps, just in time!
Good timing. The sun waited for you.
Do you know who turns the lamps on?
Nobody. They just know. Like you and laps.
Morning, Marcel! Save me a croissant!
Inès! How are you not puffing?
I am puffing! On the inside! Keep going!
Huff away, dear. It suits you.
Yusuf! Is Biscuit faster than me?
Only past the bakery. He has priorities.
Asgeir! What is tired in Norwegian?
Sliten. But you look the opposite.
Lucie! Race you to the bakery!
